title: FAST-NUCES Campuses Compared: Lahore, Islamabad, Karachi, Peshawar, CFD & Multan
excerpt: FAST-NUCES now runs six campuses, and they aren't interchangeable in seats, competition, or program mix. Here's how to think about choosing between them — including the newest one, Multan.

content.text: A detail that surprises a lot of first-time applicants: applying to "FAST" isn't a single decision. FAST-NUCES now operates six campuses — Lahore, Islamabad, Karachi, Peshawar, Chiniot-Faisalabad (CFD), and the newest addition, Multan — and when you apply, you're generally choosing which campus (or campuses) you want to be considered for, not just applying to "FAST" as one undifferentiated pool.

This matters because merit lists, seat availability, and even which programs are offered can differ from campus to campus. Treating them as six separate options rather than one option with six locations changes how you should approach both your application strategy and your expectations.

A number of guides and calculators online still describe FAST as having five campuses and leave Multan out entirely — that information is outdated. Confirm current campus options, program availability, and admission details directly at nu.edu.pk before relying on any older comparison, including ones you may find elsewhere.
Why closing merit differs by campus

Because each campus maintains its own merit list, the score needed to get in can vary meaningfully between campuses in a given year — driven by how many students apply to each one and how many seats each has for a given program. A campus that's newer or geographically less central to where most applicants live has historically tended to see lower application volume relative to seats, which can translate into a different closing merit than the older, larger campuses.

Exact closing merits, seat counts, and program availability change every admission cycle and differ by campus — always check the current year's official merit lists and prospectus at nu.edu.pk rather than relying on last year's numbers.
What actually differs between the campuses

items: Location and commute: if you're not planning to relocate, your home city may effectively decide this for you before merit even enters the picture

Program availability: not every campus necessarily offers the exact same mix of CS, Software Engineering, AI, and Engineering programs — confirm the specific program is offered at the specific campus you're targeting

Campus size and age: Islamabad (the founding campus) and Lahore are among FAST's oldest and largest; CFD is comparatively newer, and Multan is the newest of all six — which affects everything from hostel capacity to how established the range of student societies and industry connections are
Competition level: application volume (and therefore closing merit) tends to track population density and campus reputation in that specific region, not the university's overall reputation

content.text: Where Multan fits into the picture

Multan is FAST's sixth and newest campus, built to extend the university's reach into South Punjab — a region that previously meant a longer relocation for students wanting a FAST-branded CS or engineering degree. Because it's the newest campus, it's realistic to expect a few practical differences from the older, established campuses: a smaller alumni network so far, industry and internship connections still being built out, and possibly fewer years of past-paper and merit-list history to reference when estimating your own chances.

None of that makes Multan a lesser choice on paper — the entry test, merit formula, and core curriculum are the same across every FAST campus, so the degree itself carries the same weight. What differs is the surrounding ecosystem: a campus's local industry ties and alumni presence tend to build up over years, and a brand-new campus simply hasn't had that time yet. For a student from South Punjab specifically, the tradeoff is genuinely worth weighing — a much shorter commute and lower relocation cost, against a still-developing campus community compared to Lahore or Islamabad.
Choosing between campuses when you have options

If your FSc result and entry test score make you competitive at more than one FAST campus, the decision becomes less about "which FAST is best" and more about weighing location, hostel or commute logistics, and — if it matters to you — the specific student community and industry connections built up at that campus over time. A campus closer to home might mean lower living costs and family support during a demanding degree, while a campus in a bigger, more established tech hub might mean easier access to internships during your degree.

It's worth being honest with yourself here rather than defaulting to "the biggest name" — a CS degree from any FAST campus carries the same core curriculum and university name, and the meaningful differences are more about your day-to-day experience and access than about which diploma looks more impressive later.
Applying to more than one campus

Since campuses are evaluated separately, applying to more than one where you're eligible is generally a reasonable hedge rather than something to avoid — it gives you more shots at a seat without meaningfully hurting your chances at any single campus. If you're unsure which campuses accept applications together versus separately in the current cycle's application form, that's worth confirming directly rather than assuming based on past years, since application processes do get updated — and with a sixth campus now in the mix, it's worth double-checking the current application form reflects that.

Whichever campus you're targeting, the entry test and merit formula work identically across all six — so your prep strategy doesn't need to change based on campus choice, only your application logistics do.

items.question: How many campuses does FAST-NUCES have?
items.answer: Six: Islamabad (the founding campus), Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Chiniot-Faisalabad (CFD), and the newest, Multan. Some older guides and calculators still list only five and omit Multan — that information is outdated.

items.question: Is the FAST Multan campus fully operational?
items.answer: Yes — it runs its own admissions, has an active student community, and functions as FAST's sixth campus, though as the newest one it has a smaller alumni network and less-established industry connections than the older campuses so far.

items.question: Does the entry test or merit formula differ by campus?
items.answer: No — the entry test and merit formula are the same across all six campuses. What differs by campus is program availability, seat counts, and closing merit, not the test or formula itself.

items.question: Can I apply to more than one FAST campus at once?
items.answer: Generally yes, since each campus maintains a separate merit list — applying to more than one where you're eligible is a reasonable way to increase your chances without hurting your odds at any single campus. Confirm the current application form's process directly, since it can change between cycles.

items.question: Which FAST campus has the lowest closing merit?
items.answer: This varies by year and program, and generally tracks application volume relative to seats — newer or less central campuses have historically tended to see lower application volume, which can mean a different closing merit than the older, larger campuses. Always check the current year's official merit lists rather than relying on past trends.
